summary: Tenant experiencing intermittent 95th-percentile latency spikes after applying aggressive optimizer policy — guided drillback requested
description: Issue summary: Customer reported sudden increases in 95th and 99th percentile token generation latency within their tenant after we applied a new optimizer policy that combined aggressive per-op quantization (q4_0 aggressive thresholds) with early KV prefetch and larger default batch sizes. Impact: Intermittent spikes for user-facing chat endpoints (95th up to 1.8s from baseline ~350ms), increased timeouts and a handful of 502s from the serving runtime. Affects production traffic for a single enterprise tenant (NimbleHealth) on us-east. Timeline: 2026-03-09 03:14 UTC - new optimizer policy rolled to tenant via console rollout (canary 10% -> 100% over ~45m). 2026-03-09 03:50 UTC - first latency alert (95p > 1s). 2026-03-09 04:10 UTC - customer reports degraded UX. 2026-03-10 - Support ticket opened. Change details: optimizer policy id: opt-policy-nh-20260309. Main flags: quant_profile=aggressive-q4, kv_prefetch=enabled(window=8), batch_policy=auto(max_tokens=4096, bucket_ms=50). Customer note: this change was requested to reduce per-token cost and improve throughput for long context workloads. They are willing to roll back but asked for a guided sequence that minimizes request failures and avoids unsafe mass restarts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant creds for NimbleHealth and send a stream-heavy chat workload with long contexts (~4k tokens). 2) Ensure tenant optimizer policy is opt-policy-nh-20260309 applied. 3) Observe tail latency at 95/99 percentiles; reproduce with moderate concurrency (10-20 concurrent sessions) and message size distribution similar to customer (30% long messages). 4) Compare against same workload with previous policy (opt-policy-nh-20260222) where 95p was ~300-400ms.
logs:
Excerpt from serving runtime (2026-03-09T03:48:13Z): [warn] kv_prefetch miss rate rising: tenant=nh, miss_rate=0.42, avg_prefetch_latency_ms=26.3; [error] scheduler: deferred token slot exhaustion: tenant=nh, queue_depth=78, max_concurrent_streams=64; [info] quantizer: applied aggressive-q4 rewrite: model=redwood-vicuna-13b-q4, expected_mem_saving=34% but observed tail_cpu_ms=+18.
HTTP 502 sample: timestamp=2026-03-09T03:51:02Z, route=/v1/chat/stream, status=502, upstream_err=serve-timeout
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) aggressive quantization increases CPU/GPU kernel variance leading to jitter on long sequences (observed +18ms tail per-op). 2) KV prefetch window of 8 is causing extra scheduling pressure and increased queueing under certain token distributions. 3) Larger bucket_ms and max_tokens allow batching to group heterogeneous sequences, increasing head-of-line blocking for short requests. What we ran: - Controlled repro in staging with opt-policy-nh-20260309 and a synthetic distribution: reproduced 95p spike at 1.6s. - Flipped kv_prefetch=disabled in staging for the policy: 95p dropped ~400ms. - Reduced batch bucket_ms to 15ms and max_tokens to 2048: observed overall reduction in tail but small throughput impact. - Compared CPU/GPU timelines: saw more frequent kernel resubmissions correlated with quant profile. Initial conclusion: interaction between aggressive-q4 quant profile and kv_prefetch under existing batching settings causes queuing and kernel variance.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket created after NimbleHealth reached out. Collected traces, logs and initial metrics. Noted rollout ID and config. Requested escalation to SRE and optimizer team.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Marco Gonzalez): Confirmed 95p spikes in tenant namespace. Spun up staging repro. Asked product to prepare safe drillback steps that don't require rolling restarts of all serving pods.

2026-03-11 - Optimizer Eng (Lydia Chen): Suggested prioritized disable of kv_prefetch first because it was the lowest-risk toggle in the chain. Sent a CLI snippet to apply a per-tenant override. Also asked for customer workload sample for further simulation.

2026-03-11 - NimbleHealth (support@nimblehealth.com): Provided recent chat logs and agreed to a temporary throughput reduction if it stabilizes latency. Asked for sequence to allow graceful in-flight request handling.
2026-03-12 - Marco Gonzalez: Performed a controlled override for 10% of tenant traffic: kv_prefetch=false. Early metrics show 95p falling ~350ms on canary subset. Preparing wider roll out guidance.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with recommended rollback plan and asked CS to confirm business acceptance of brief throughput hit during full backout.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation (in-progress): staged per-tenant override to disable kv_prefetch (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and reduce batch bucket_ms to 25ms for the tenant. Observed 95p improvement on canary. Recommended full backout sequence (safe drillback) — guidance below: 1) Apply per-tenant override: set kv_prefetch=false for opt-policy-nh-20260309. 2) Decrease batch_policy.bucket_ms to 25 and max_tokens to 3072 to reduce head-of-line blocking. 3) Keep aggressive quant_profile in place during initial canary to evaluate tail variance; if 95/99p still elevated after kv_prefetch off, flip quant_profile to conservative-q4 (or the previous exact profile id opt-qprofile-20260222). 4) Validate on 10% traffic for 15-30 minutes, monitor tail and 5xxs; then promote to 50% and finally 100% with monitoring gates. 5) If customer requests immediate full revert, apply a per-tenant model pin to the previous non-quantized model (redwood-vicuna-13b:rev-20260222) as a last-resort fast rollback because model pinning is stateless from serving perspective. Operational notes: - Avoid cluster-wide restarts; these toggles are per-tenant and hot-applied. - Expect a temporary throughput loss ~5-15% when reducing batching. - Notify CS and customer with exact change window and monitoring links. Follow-ups: create an automated canary playbook for this class of optimizer interactions, add a unit test to optimizer config validation that flags aggressive quant + kv_prefetch combinations for tenants with >2k token contexts.
next_steps: 1) CS to confirm acceptance of staged canary backout window (requested: 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC). 2) SRE to run canary rollout on production with close monitoring (Marco). 3) Optimizer team to create a config lint rule to prevent this combination for enterprise tenants by default. 4) Schedule post-action review and add runbook entry.
public_customer_message: We are working with you to reverse the recent optimizer changes safely. Our immediate step is to disable the KV prefetch feature for your tenant and temporarily reduce batching aggressiveness to stabilize response times. This will slightly increase per-token cost and may reduce throughput for a short window while we validate. We'll coordinate exact timing and monitor in real time.
